For a collective multi-host event, secondary hosts' events would be created against the first host's calendar (or filtered out). This is a real, verifiable incompleteness exposed by this diff; confidence moderate because the collective flow reaching these services isn't fully visible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` for collective/team scenarios. However, `BaseCalendarService` (iCal) still does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and filters/marks primary calendars only against that first element (e.g. `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` around the shown hunks), with no per-credential/per-destination selection. Likewise, Lark and Office365 services also destructure only the first element to choose `calendarId`/URL. This means when `destinationCalendar` contains multiple hosts, non-Google integrations will still target only the first destination (or potentially create duplicates in the first calendar), so the multi-host collective fix is effectively incomplete outside Google and can produce incorrect behavior.
